standard.name: The Sanitation System Management Standard, Part 1 - Asset Management

assetTypes.name: Sanitation system
assetTypes.description: Collection of assets that work together as a system to contain, collect, transport, treat, and safely dispose of or reuse wastewater and faecal sludge

assetTypes.name: Subsystem
assetTypes.description: Functional or administrative subdivision of a larger sanitation system

assetTypes.name: Facility
assetTypes.description: Physical location where specific functions are performed in the collection, transport, treatment, disposal, or reuse of wastewater and faecal sludge; optional, used to organize or locate the assets contained in large and complex systems.

assetTypes.name: Sanitation point
assetTypes.description: Location or facility where users access sanitation services, including toilets, latrines, urinals, and communal or public sanitation blocks

assetTypes.name: Connection
assetTypes.description: Property or customer location that receives sanitation service

assetTypes.name: Containment
assetTypes.description: Structure that holds excreta and wastewater at or near where they are generated; some types also provide partial treatment

assetTypes.name: Vehicle
assetTypes.description: Mobile asset used to empty, transport, or transfer faecal sludge, septage, or wastewater

assetTypes.name: Manhole
assetTypes.description: Structure that provides access to a sewer for inspection, cleaning, and maintenance; includes inspection chambers and cleanouts

assetTypes.name: Junction
assetTypes.description: Section of a piped network that joins two or more pipes or conduits

assetTypes.name: Valve
assetTypes.description: Mechanical device designed to close off or regulate the flow of wastewater, sludge, air, or other fluids in a pipe or closed conduit

assetTypes.name: Flow control
assetTypes.description: Structure or device that diverts, splits, restricts, releases, or measures flow in an open channel or basin

assetTypes.name: Structure
assetTypes.description: Anything that is constructed or built with a fixed location on the ground

assetTypes.name: Power
assetTypes.description: Device that supplies electrical power for use by electrical equipment, such as a generator, solar power system, wind turbine, or connection to a power grid

assetTypes.name: Electrical
assetTypes.description: Electrical or electronic device

assetTypes.name: Meter
assetTypes.description: Device for measuring the flow rate of wastewater, effluent, or sludge through a pipe or open channel

assetTypes.name: Sampling point
assetTypes.description: Location or access point that allows a sample of influent, effluent, sludge, or receiving water to be collected for testing

assetTypes.name: Sensor
assetTypes.description: Device that measures a physical condition or parameter of interest

assetTypes.name: Analyzer
assetTypes.description: Device that conducts periodic or continuous measurements of a wastewater, effluent, or process quality parameter

assetTypes.name: Datalogger
assetTypes.description: Device that automatically records measurements over time from connected sensors, meters, or analyzers, and stores the data locally or transmits it to a remote system

assetTypes.name: Pump
assetTypes.description: Mechanical or electromechanical device that increases the hydraulic head (pressure) of a fluid flowing through it

assetTypes.name: Tank
assetTypes.description: Structure or container used to hold wastewater, sludge, chemicals, or other fluids within a conveyance network or treatment facility; on-site vessels such as septic tanks are classified under Containment

assetTypes.name: Treatment
assetTypes.description: Equipment or process unit that improves the physical, chemical, or biological quality of wastewater or faecal sludge, including separation, stabilization, and dewatering of solids

assetTypes.name: Dispersal
assetTypes.description: Structure that discharges treated or partially treated effluent to the soil for infiltration and/or evapotranspiration

assetTypes.name: Outfall
assetTypes.description: Point or structure where effluent, overflow, or emergency discharge leaves the system and enters a receiving water body or the environment

assetTypes.name: Other vertical
assetTypes.description: Any other type of vertical asset not defined elsewhere in this standard

assetTypes.name: Pipe
assetTypes.description: Conduit that carries wastewater, sludge, or other fluids from one location to another

assetTypes.name: Channel
assetTypes.description: Artificial open or covered channel constructed to convey wastewater, effluent, or combined flows from one location to another. Includes natural watercourses that have been substantially modified (lined, regraded, or walled) and are managed as part of the system

attributes.name: Type
attributes.description: Type of asset

attributes.name: Name
attributes.description: Name used by technical staff to refer to the asset; might be left blank for many lower level assets

attributes.name: Unique ID
attributes.description: Unique number automatically assigned when creating an asset

attributes.name: Description
attributes.description: Additional information to help staff locate or identify an asset

attributes.name: Photo
attributes.description: Photos of the asset

attributes.name: Parent asset
attributes.description: Asset ID of the asset that is a parent to this asset

attributes.name: Location
attributes.description: Geographic location of the asset on the surface of the Earth; may be a point, line, or polygon

attributes.name: Location precision
attributes.description: Estimated uncertainty in the geographic coordinates, expressed as a distance

attributes.name: Survey elevation
attributes.description: Height above a reference surface, as measured by surveying or high-precision GNSS equipment; used for hydraulic modeling and engineering design. This value is distinct from the altitude captured automatically with GPS coordinates. For chambered assets such as manholes, the surveyed point is the center of the cover

attributes.name: Survey elevation datum
attributes.description: Vertical reference system used for Survey elevation and Invert level values

choices.name: Ellipsoid (WGS84)
choices.description: Height above the WGS84 reference ellipsoid, as reported by GNSS receivers

choices.name: Mean sea level
choices.description: Height above local mean sea level or a national vertical datum

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other vertical reference system; describe in Additional technical details

attributes.name: Elevation precision
attributes.description: Estimated uncertainty in the measurement of the elevation

attributes.name: Administrative region
attributes.description: Name that describes the administrative geography of the location; multiple levels may be separated by commas starting with the most general area, for example: Region, District, Municipality

attributes.name: Coverage area
attributes.description: Geographical area where the sanitation system or service provides coverage or is legally obligated to serve

attributes.name: Sector
attributes.description: Name for a sub-region of the coverage area that is defined by geography or the physical layout of the collection network

attributes.name: Route
attributes.description: Name or number of the service route, such as a scheduled emptying (desludging) route, which defines the assets assigned to a particular staff member or team

attributes.name: Address
attributes.description: Physical address or postal address where the asset is located; in the case of sewer or property connections, the address of the customer

attributes.name: Urban-rural classification
attributes.description: Degree of urbanization, as defined by national standards or the Degree of Urbanisation method (OECD 2021)

choices.name: Urban
choices.description: Cities or densely populated areas

choices.name: Peri urban
choices.description: Towns and semi-dense areas, suburbs, or peri urban areas surrounding cities

choices.name: Rural
choices.description: Regions with low population density

attributes.name: Community
attributes.description: Name of the community, town, or neighborhood where a sanitation system or facility is located

attributes.name: Accessible by road
attributes.description: Asset can be accessed by vehicles using a nearby road

attributes.name: Perimeter fence or wall installed
attributes.description: Fence or wall exists to provide physical security for the asset

attributes.name: Wheelchair accessible
attributes.description: Asset can be accessed and used by people using wheelchairs or with limited mobility

attributes.name: Distance to nearest water source
attributes.description: Distance from the containment or dispersal structure to the nearest well, borehole, spring, or other groundwater source used for drinking water

attributes.name: Land occupancy
attributes.description: Legal status of the land the asset occupies or crosses
attributes.applicability: All types except: Sanitation system, subsystem

choices.name: Public or utility land
choices.description: Asset lies in public land, a road reserve, or land owned or controlled by the service provider

choices.name: Private land, with agreement
choices.description: Asset crosses land owned by others, with a documented easement, right-of-way, or written agreement

choices.name: Private land, without agreement
choices.description: Asset crosses land owned by others without a documented arrangement, such as informal or customary permission

choices.name: Unknown
choices.description: Land status has not been determined

attributes.name: Level 1
attributes.description: Highest or most general level of categorization to which the asset belongs under the asset hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 2
attributes.description: Second highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 3
attributes.description: Third highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 4
attributes.description: Fourth highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 5
attributes.description: Fifth highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 6
attributes.description: Sixth highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 7
attributes.description: Lowest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Status
attributes.description: How the asset is currently being used or operated

choices.name: Active
choices.description: Asset is in use or ready to use

choices.name: Backup
choices.description: Asset is installed or available onsite to be used as a backup to other similar assets in case of maintenance or failure

choices.name: Not functional
choices.description: Asset is not currently operational due to a failure or maintenance problem

choices.name: Under construction
choices.description: Asset is not operational because it is under construction

choices.name: Decommissioned
choices.description: Asset is no longer in use because it is permanently out of service

choices.name: Disposed
choices.description: Asset has been sold, demolished, or relocated to a disposal site

attributes.name: Condition
attributes.description: The physical or structural integrity of the asset

choices.name: Excellent
choices.description: Designed to current standards, operable and well-maintained

choices.name: Good
choices.description: Showing some signs of minor wear and tear, with minimal impact on performance; or, operable and well-maintained but not designed to current standards

choices.name: Fair
choices.description: Structurally sound but some deterioration or damage that is beginning to impact performance or require more frequent maintenance

choices.name: Poor
choices.description: Functional but requires a high level of maintenance to continue operating or requires major rehabilitation or replacement

choices.name: Very poor
choices.description: Serious problems that impact performance or safety; major rehabilitation or replacement required in the short term

attributes.name: Functional status
attributes.description: Most recent observation of whether a sanitation system or sanitation point is working as designed

choices.name: Functional
choices.description: In good working condition and regularly providing service according to the specifications in the original design

choices.name: Partially functional
choices.description: Provides service on a regular basis (possibly in a reduced capacity) but repairs are needed due to some maintenance or structural issue

choices.name: Not functional
choices.description: No longer providing service on a regular basis; this could be due to maintenance issues, structural failure, or problems with physical access

choices.name: Decommissioned
choices.description: Permanently taken out of service, abandoned, or could not be found

attributes.name: Current replacement cost (USD)
attributes.description: Cost (in US Dollars) that would be incurred to replace the asset at the current time; this value requires regular updating based on depreciation and current market conditions; also known as CRC

attributes.name: Expected useful life
attributes.description: Number of years that the asset is estimated to function after installation if it is well maintained; also known as EUL

attributes.name: Probability of failure
attributes.description: Measure of the likelihood of a failure happening at any point in time, based on an analysis of the potential failure modes of the asset

attributes.name: Consequence of failure
attributes.description: Measure of the direct and indirect costs of asset failure, which may include financial, environmental, and societal costs

attributes.name: Asset risk
attributes.description: Business or organizational risk of asset failure, usually calculated from the probability and consequence of failure

attributes.name: Original cost (USD)
attributes.description: Total price paid (in US Dollars) to initially acquire an asset

attributes.name: Current rehabilitation cost (USD)
attributes.description: Cost (in US Dollars) that would be incurred to rehabilitate the asset at the current time

attributes.name: Manufacturer
attributes.description: Name of the business that produced or sold the asset
attributes.applicability: Type: Pump, Tank, Power, Meter, Electrical, Valve, Sensor, Analyzer, Vehicle, Connection, Datalogger, Treatment, Containment, Manhole

attributes.name: Model
attributes.description: Manufacturer's designation for the particular model of the asset
attributes.applicability: Type: Pump, Tank, Power, Meter, Electrical, Valve, Sensor, Analyzer, Vehicle, Connection, Datalogger, Treatment, Containment, Manhole

attributes.name: Serial number
attributes.description: Unique identifying number or code assigned to a particular asset by the manufacturer or vendor, usually stamped or printed on the asset
attributes.applicability: Type: Pump, Tank, Power, Meter, Electrical, Valve, Sensor, Analyzer, Vehicle, Connection, Datalogger, Treatment, Containment, Manhole

attributes.name: Additional technical details
attributes.description: Any other technical information about the asset that is not captured by the attributes of this standard

attributes.name: Installation date
attributes.description: Calendar date when the asset was installed or purchased, which begins the period of useful life

attributes.name: Installed by
attributes.description: Name of the company or organization that originally installed or purchased the asset

attributes.name: Funded by
attributes.description: Name of the funding authority, lender, or donor who funded the purchase of the system or facility

attributes.name: Rehabilitation date
attributes.description: Date of most recent work done to restore the asset to its original level of service and extend its life

attributes.name: Last service date
attributes.description: Date of most recent service or maintenance performed; for containment assets, the date of most recent emptying

attributes.name: Last calibration date
attributes.description: Calendar date when the device was last calibrated against a known reference or standard solution

attributes.name: Rehabilitated by
attributes.description: Name of the company or organization that performed the most recent rehabilitation of the asset

attributes.name: Service interval
attributes.description: Recommended interval at which service or routine maintenance should be performed on the asset, such as the scheduled emptying frequency of a containment asset or the calibration of a measuring device
attributes.applicability: All types except: Sanitation system, Subsystem, Facility, Connection

attributes.name: Date of manufacture
attributes.description: Calendar date when the asset was manufactured
attributes.applicability: Type: Pump, Tank, Power, Meter, Electrical, Valve, Sensor, Analyzer, Vehicle, Connection, Datalogger

attributes.name: Decommissioning date
attributes.description: Calendar date when the asset was permanently taken out of service

attributes.name: Owner
attributes.description: Name of the individual, organization, or authority that holds legal ownership of the asset, which may differ from the organization that operates or manages it

attributes.name: Operator
attributes.description: Name of the individual, organization, or authority that operates or maintains the asset, if different from the owner; assets without an operator recorded are assumed to be operated by their parent system's operator
attributes.applicability: Type: Sanitation system, Facility, Sanitation point, Vehicle

attributes.name: Upstream asset
attributes.description: Asset ID of the upstream asset from which this asset receives flow
attributes.applicability: Type: Pump, Tank, Treatment, Meter, Valve, Flow control, Junction, Sampling point, Sanitation point, Containment, Manhole, Dispersal, Outfall, Pipe, Channel, Connection

attributes.name: Downstream asset
attributes.description: Asset ID of the downstream asset that receives flow from this asset
attributes.applicability: Type: Pump, Tank, Treatment, Meter, Valve, Flow control, Junction, Sampling point, Sanitation point, Containment, Manhole, Dispersal, Outfall, Pipe, Channel, Connection

attributes.name: Nominal diameter
attributes.description: An approximate measurement of the internal diameter of a pipe, conduit, pump, or junction, which is used to classify according to standard sizes
attributes.applicability: Type: Meter, Valve, Junction, Pipe, Connection

attributes.name: Pipe length
attributes.description: Total length of the pipe itself, measured along its slope from the start to the end of the pipe and excluding manhole chambers, for use in hydraulic calculations and modeling

attributes.name: Material
attributes.description: Material of construction for pipes, junctions, chambers, and other conduits
attributes.applicability: Type: Meter, Valve, Junction, Pipe, Manhole, Containment, Channel

choices.name: Cast iron
choices.description: Heavy brittle alloy of iron, carbon, and silicon that can be cast in specific shapes and has the ability to withstand shocks

choices.name: Ductile iron
choices.description: Similar material to cast iron, but with the primary graphite in a nodular or spheroidal form, giving it increased strength and flexibility

choices.name: Steel
choices.description: Iron-base alloy containing up to 2 percent carbon that is heat treated

choices.name: Stainless steel
choices.description: Chromium alloy steel that is resistant to rusting and corrosion

choices.name: Galvanized steel
choices.description: Steel that has a zinc coating to protect from corrosion and rust

choices.name: Vitrified clay
choices.description: Clay pipe fired at high temperature to form a chemically inert, corrosion-resistant material widely used in gravity sewers

choices.name: Concrete
choices.description: Mixture of cement and aggregate, usually reinforced with steel wire or rebar; includes reinforced concrete pipe and cast-in-place chambers

choices.name: Masonry
choices.description: Brick, stone, or concrete blocks that are bound together with mortar; common in legacy trunk sewers and chambers

choices.name: Asbestos cement
choices.description: Cement reinforced with asbestos fibers, found in legacy pipelines; subject to handling and disposal safety precautions

choices.name: Fiberglass (GRP)
choices.description: Reinforced plastic material composed of glass fibers embedded within a resin matrix; also known as glass-reinforced plastic

choices.name: PVC
choices.description: Polyvinyl chloride, a type of polymer frequently used in pipes and containers

choices.name: HDPE
choices.description: High-density polyethylene, a type of polymer used in gravity and pressure pipelines

choices.name: Plastic
choices.description: Any high molecular weight polymer material that can be extruded, molded, or drawn into various shapes and sizes; use this category for any plastics that are not PVC or HDPE

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any material not otherwise defined in this section

attributes.name: Minor loss coefficient
attributes.description: Dimensionless coefficient that can be used to account for the head loss associated with turbulence in bends, junctions, meters, and valves; usually applicable to pressurized (rising) mains

attributes.name: Roughness coefficient
attributes.description: Dimensionless coefficient used to account for friction losses in flowing conduits, such as Manning's n for gravity sewers and open channels or Hazen-Williams C for pressurized mains

attributes.name: Conveyed content
attributes.description: Primary type of flow or material conveyed or handled by the asset
attributes.applicability: Type: Pump, Tank, Valve, Flow control, Meter, Junction, Sampling point, Manhole, Outfall, Pipe, Channel

choices.name: Wastewater
choices.description: Untreated wastewater, including domestic sewage and blackwater

choices.name: Blackwater
choices.description: Wastewater from toilets containing excreta, with or without flushwater, conveyed separately from other streams

choices.name: Greywater
choices.description: Wastewater from washing, bathing, laundry, and food preparation that does not contain excreta

choices.name: Treated effluent
choices.description: Liquid stream that has undergone treatment prior to discharge or reuse

choices.name: Sludge or septage
choices.description: Sludge from treatment processes, or sludge and liquid mixtures emptied from on-site containment (faecal sludge)

choices.name: Combined sewage and stormwater
choices.description: Mixture of wastewater and stormwater conveyed in a combined sewer

choices.name: Stormwater
choices.description: Rainfall runoff only; assets dedicated solely to stormwater drainage are outside the scope of this standard

choices.name: Biogas
choices.description: Gas produced by anaerobic digestion, conveyed for recovery, use, or flaring

choices.name: Air
choices.description: Air conveyed for aeration, ventilation, or odor control

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other conveyed content not defined in this section

attributes.name: Invert level
attributes.description: Elevation of the lowest point of the internal surface of a channel or chamber, recorded against the same datum as Survey elevation

attributes.name: Primary contact name
attributes.description: Individual or office responsible for management or administration of the sanitation system or sanitation point
attributes.applicability: Type: Sanitation system,Subsystem, Facility, Sanitation point

attributes.name: Primary contact position
attributes.description: Title or role in the organization of the primary contact
attributes.applicability: Type: Sanitation system,Subsystem, Facility, Sanitation point

attributes.name: Primary contact phone number
attributes.description: Phone number of the primary contact
attributes.applicability: Type: Sanitation system,Subsystem, Facility, Sanitation point

attributes.name: Secondary contact name
attributes.description: Additional individual who may be contacted if the primary contact is not available
attributes.applicability: Type: Sanitation system,Subsystem, Facility, Sanitation point

attributes.name: Secondary contact position
attributes.description: Title or role of the secondary contact
attributes.applicability: Type: Sanitation system,Subsystem, Facility, Sanitation point

attributes.name: Secondary contact phone number
attributes.description: Phone number of the secondary contact
attributes.applicability: Type: Sanitation system,Subsystem, Facility, Sanitation point

attributes.name: Date updated
attributes.description: Calendar date of the most recent update made to any attribute

attributes.name: Date inspected
attributes.description: Calendar date of the most recent inspection or audit of the asset, as defined by organizational asset management policies

attributes.name: Alternate ID
attributes.description: Optional additional identification code or number that is used by other data systems or organizations to track the asset

attributes.name: Import code
attributes.description: Identification code for an asset that was assigned by an external database or asset management registry, used to maintain backwards traceability for assets that have been imported

attributes.name: Permit or licence number
attributes.description: Identification number of the primary permit, licence, or registration issued for the asset by a regulator or government authority
attributes.applicability: Type: Sanitation system, Facility, Sanitation point, Vehicle, Outfall

attributes.name: Sanitation system type
attributes.description: Categorization of the system by how excreta and wastewater are contained and conveyed: through a sewer network, in on-site containment, or both

choices.name: Sewered
choices.description: Piped sewer network that removes excreta and wastewater from the premises where they are produced and carries them to treatment or a discharge point

choices.name: Non-sewered (on-site)
choices.description: Excreta and wastewater are contained at or near the point of generation, with or without subsequent emptying, transport, and off-site treatment

choices.name: Mixed
choices.description: System serves users through both sewered and non-sewered services within its coverage area

attributes.name: Sewer network type
attributes.description: Categorization of the collecting network by what it is designed to carry: wastewater only in separate sewers, wastewater and stormwater together in combined sewers, or both

choices.name: Separate
choices.description: Collecting network conveying primarily sanitary wastewater, with stormwater excluded or carried separately; also known as sanitary or foul sewers

choices.name: Combined
choices.description: Network that carries sanitary wastewater and also receives stormwater or snowmelt during wet weather

choices.name: Both separate and combined
choices.description: Collecting network contains both separate and combined sections

attributes.name: Management type
attributes.description: Type of organization that manages the operations, maintenance, and finances of the sanitation system

choices.name: Utility
choices.description: Organization created by government through legislative action or a private partnership or corporation with a legal mandate to provide sanitation services to a designated area

choices.name: Local government
choices.description: Local or municipal government office or staff directly manage the system

choices.name: Community-based organization
choices.description: Community-based organization, committee, or cooperative group of users that manages the system (also known as community-based management)

choices.name: Sanitation authority
choices.description: Government agency or regulatory body established for the purpose of managing sanitation service provision

choices.name: Private
choices.description: Individual, partnership, or corporation that owns and operates a sanitation system but does not have a legal mandate to provide services to all users in an area

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other management entity not described by the other choices

choices.name: No management
choices.description: No individual or organization can be identified that manages the system

attributes.name: Number of households in service area
attributes.description: Total number of households within the area that a service provider is legally mandated to offer services to

attributes.name: Number of households currently served
attributes.description: Number of households currently receiving service, whether through a functional sewer connection or through regular servicing of on-site containment (includes households with inactive, intermittent, or cut off service, if service could be re-established)

attributes.name: System or network diagram
attributes.description: Photograph of a recent map or diagram showing the location of sanitation infrastructure, such as the collection network and treatment assets

attributes.name: Total treatment capacity
attributes.description: Indicative amount of wastewater and faecal sludge that the system's treatment assets are able to receive and treat, within current resource and design constraints

attributes.name: Sewer technology
attributes.description: Predominant sewer technology used in the collecting network

choices.name: Conventional gravity
choices.description: Gravity sewers laid at self-cleansing gradients and conventional depths, typically in public rights-of-way, with manhole access

choices.name: Simplified or condominial
choices.description: Smaller-diameter gravity sewers laid at shallower depths and reduced gradients, with simplified access chambers, often following shortened routes including through private property

choices.name: Settled (small-bore)
choices.description: Small-diameter sewers conveying settled, solids-free effluent from interceptor or septic tanks

choices.name: Pressure
choices.description: Sewers pressurized by pumps, such as grinder pump or septic tank effluent pump (STEP) systems

choices.name: Vacuum
choices.description: Network kept under negative pressure by a central vacuum station, with interface valves at connections

choices.name: Mixed
choices.description: Network combines more than one sewer technology

attributes.name: Design capacity (population equivalent)
attributes.description: Design capacity of the system expressed in population equivalent (p.e.), a standardized load unit where 1 p.e. is an organic biodegradable load with a five-day biochemical oxygen demand (BOD₅) of 60 g of oxygen per day, independent of actual local per-capita loads (Directive (EU) 2024/3019, Art. 2(10))

attributes.name: Facility type
attributes.description: Type of physical location where a specific function is performed in the collection, transport, treatment, or disposal/reuse of wastewater and faecal sludge

choices.name: Wastewater treatment plant
choices.description: Facility containing treatment works and process areas that treat sewered wastewater to an acceptable standard before discharge or reuse

choices.name: Faecal sludge treatment plant
choices.description: Facility designed to receive and treat faecal sludge delivered from on-site containment

choices.name: Pumping or lift station
choices.description: Structure containing pumps and related piping used to convey wastewater or faecal sludge

choices.name: Transfer station
choices.description: Facility where faecal sludge from small-scale collection is transferred to larger transport for onward conveyance

choices.name: Storage facility
choices.description: One or more tanks used to store wastewater, effluent, or faecal sludge

choices.name: Process area
choices.description: Area or building, often within a treatment plant, where a specific treatment process is carried out

choices.name: Retention or detention facility
choices.description: Basin or structure that temporarily holds flows, such as combined sewer overflow or equalization storage

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of facility not defined in this section

attributes.name: Process area type
attributes.description: Optional label used to categorize process areas within a facility

attributes.name: Equipped to receive faecal sludge
attributes.description: The treatment facility is equipped to receive faecal sludge or septage delivered by vehicle, in addition to sewered flow, such as through a discharge structure or receiving station

attributes.name: Sanitation point type
attributes.description: Type of technology used by the sanitation point to collect user excreta across sewered and non-sewered systems

choices.name: Flush/pour-flush toilet
choices.description: Toilet with a water seal, flushed by a cistern or by pouring water by hand, discharging to a sewer, septic tank, or pit

choices.name: Pit latrine with slab
choices.description: Dry toilet over a pit, covered by a durable, cleanable slab or platform with a drop hole or seat

choices.name: Pit latrine without slab or open pit
choices.description: Dry toilet over a pit lacking a durable slab, platform, or seat

attributes.name: Treatment type
attributes.description: Categorization of treatment process by treatment method or objective, spanning liquid-stream (wastewater) and sludge/faecal sludge treatment technologies

choices.name: Screen
choices.description: Bar rack, mesh, or fine screen at the headworks that intercepts coarse solids, rags, and debris carried in the incoming flow

choices.name: Grit removal
choices.description: Channel, vortex unit, or aerated chamber at the headworks in which sand, gravel, and other dense inorganic particles settle out of the flow

choices.name: Grease or FOG removal
choices.description: Trap, skimming chamber, or flotation unit at the headworks that separates fats, oils, and grease from the flow

choices.name: Sedimentation or settler
choices.description: Tank or basin in which settleable solids separate from wastewater or faecal sludge under gravity, whether ahead of or following biological treatment

choices.name: Imhoff tank
choices.description: Two-story tank combining primary sedimentation with separate sludge digestion in a lower compartment

choices.name: Anaerobic baffled reactor (ABR)
choices.description: Series of baffled chambers that direct flow up and down through settled sludge for anaerobic treatment

choices.name: Anaerobic filter
choices.description: Fixed-bed reactor in which wastewater flows through a submerged filter medium supporting anaerobic biofilm

choices.name: Upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB)
choices.description: Reactor in which wastewater flows upward through a blanket of anaerobic sludge granules for high-rate digestion

choices.name: Waste stabilization pond
choices.description: Shallow earthen pond that treats wastewater by sedimentation, digestion, and algal-bacterial processes; typically constructed in series as anaerobic, facultative, and maturation stages. Each pond in a series is registered as a separate Treatment asset, linked using upstream/downstream relationships.

choices.name: Aerated lagoon or pond
choices.description: Earthen basin in which mechanical or diffused aeration supplements natural oxygenation to treat wastewater

choices.name: Free-water surface constructed wetland
choices.description: Engineered wetland in which wastewater flows as a shallow open layer above the soil, through the stems of emergent plants, resembling a natural marsh

choices.name: Horizontal subsurface flow constructed wetland
choices.description: Engineered wetland in which wastewater moves sideways through a planted bed of gravel or sand, staying below the surface of the media

choices.name: Vertical flow constructed wetland
choices.description: Engineered wetland in which wastewater is applied to the surface in intermittent doses and drains downward through a planted media bed to collection pipes at the base

choices.name: Trickling filter
choices.description: Fixed-film reactor in which wastewater trickles over a bed of rock or plastic media colonized by microorganisms

choices.name: Rotating biological contactor (RBC)
choices.description: Series of rotating discs partially submerged in wastewater that support a biofilm for aerobic treatment

choices.name: Aeration basin
choices.description: Basin in which wastewater is mixed with a suspended microbial culture and aerated to degrade organic matter

choices.name: Sequencing batch reactor (SBR)
choices.description: Single basin in which aeration, settling, and decanting of a suspended microbial culture occur in timed sequence rather than in separate units

choices.name: Membrane bioreactor (MBR)
choices.description: Basin holding a suspended microbial culture combined with membrane filtration in place of a separate settling stage

choices.name: Moving bed biofilm reactor (MBBR)
choices.description: Aerobic or anaerobic basin using free-floating plastic carriers that hold a biofilm in suspension

choices.name: Coagulation or flocculation
choices.description: Addition of chemicals with gentle mixing to destabilize and aggregate suspended particles for improved settling

choices.name: Filtration
choices.description: Granular, cloth, or membrane filter that removes residual particulates from treated effluent

choices.name: Chlorine contact tank
choices.description: Basin or vessel in which chlorine, in liquid, solid, or gaseous form, is contacted with effluent for disinfection

choices.name: UV or ozone disinfection unit
choices.description: Reactor or chamber that inactivates pathogens in effluent by non-chlorine means, such as ultraviolet light or ozone

choices.name: Chemical dosing system
choices.description: Storage, pump, and delivery equipment that doses chemicals for a treatment function such as pH control, odor control, or corrosion prevention

choices.name: Thickener
choices.description: Gravity or mechanical unit that concentrates sludge or faecal sludge solids before further treatment

choices.name: Anaerobic digester
choices.description: Enclosed reactor in which microorganisms break down sludge or faecal sludge without oxygen, often producing biogas

choices.name: Unplanted drying bed
choices.description: Shallow bed with a filtration medium that dewaters sludge or faecal sludge by drainage and evaporation

choices.name: Planted drying bed
choices.description: Drying bed planted with wetland vegetation that enhances dewatering and stabilization of sludge or faecal sludge

choices.name: Dewatering unit
choices.description: Centrifuge, belt filter press, or screw press that mechanically separates liquid from sludge or faecal sludge

choices.name: Composting pad or windrow
choices.description: Pad, windrow, or vessel in which dewatered sludge or faecal sludge is mixed with organic bulking material and composted aerobically

choices.name: Lime stabilization
choices.description: Addition of lime to raise pH and reduce pathogens in sludge or faecal sludge

choices.name: Incineration or thermal treatment
choices.description: Combustion or other thermal process that reduces sludge or faecal sludge volume and destroys pathogens

choices.name: Aerobic digester
choices.description: Open or closed tank in which sludge is aerated to stabilize solids without biogas production; common in small and package plants

choices.name: Odor control (gas treatment)
choices.description: Equipment that contains, ventilates and treats odorous gases from collection or treatment assets

choices.name: Other
